1.why: Text uses a clean sans-serif typeface with clear headings, roomy line spacing and good contrast on white cards, though letter spacing is default and code values are in dense monospace.

2.why: No italics or all-caps beyond the small 'NORTHSTAR BANK' wordmark, and body copy is limited to one- or two-line paragraphs rather than dense blocks.

3.why: The layout is a single narrow centred column with full-width fields and buttons that would fit a phone screen, although the long otpauth:// string and log panel wrap awkwardly.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Store these recovery codes somewhere secure. Each code works once.' are short and plain, but terms like 'provisioning representation' and 'manual secret' are jargon.

5.why: Only the recovery code field shows an example format placeholder ('ABCD-EFGH-JKLM'); the verification code and authenticator code fields show no example of expected input.

6.why: Each screen presents only a couple of short sentences, so no long block of text must be read to proceed.

7.why: The manual secret, otpauth string and eight recovery codes are displayed as plain text with no copy button or download option, so they must be selected or typed by hand.

8.why: No QR code image is rendered at all — only a raw 'otpauth://' text URI labelled 'Provisioning representation', which is not a scannable equivalent.

9.why: Standard login name and password inputs are used which browsers can generally autofill, but no autocomplete hints (e.g. one-time-code) or visible password-manager affordances are shown.

10.why: Each screen has a clear bold heading and a prominent green primary button, but there is no step indicator or progress marker, and step 4 shows two competing buttons ('Create authenticator secret' and 'Enable MFA').

11.why: Most screens ask one thing, yet step 4 combines creating the secret and entering a code, and step 6 offers 'Use recovery code' plus 'Generate replacement recovery codes' simultaneously.

12.why: 'MFA is enabled' confirms success and offers next links, but transitions like signing in or verifying identity give no plain confirmation, and step 7 surfaces a raw DOM exception instead of a status message.

13.why: The user can re-request a new secret, regenerate replacement recovery codes, revisit Authenticator/Recovery codes links, and retry sign-in repeatedly without lockout being shown.

14.why: Errors are unhelpful rather than blaming: 'Unable to continue sign-in.' gives no cause or fix, and "Failed to execute 'insertBefore' on 'Node'..." is a raw developer stack message; they also stack up unbounded.

15.why: No countdown timer or session expiry is visible on any screen, but the flow states codes 'rotate every 30 seconds' and the verification code is described as 'short-lived', implying an implicit time pressure.
